title: New York City outlines plan to close digital divide, expand affordable internet
summary: The draft plan features steps to deliver affordable, high-speed internet to more New Yorkers and eliminate digital inequity across the city.

title: Tennessee taps Indiana tech leader Robert Fulk for Secretary of State CIO role
summary: Fulk arrives in Tennessee after leadership roles in Indiana’s Secretary of State office, where he modernized a number of state services using AI.

title: As states move quickly to govern AI, dedicated oversight remains a challenge
summary: New NASCIO survey state AI officers navigating expanding responsibilities as governments work to establish rules for artificial intelligence.

title: Securing the source of identity: Why high-assurance proofing matters for vital records
summary: State agencies can balance constituent access and strong security by building high-assurance identity proofing into a layered ordering model.

title: Maryland launches Data Academy to strengthen state workforce’s data skills
summary: The new training platform uses personalized learning pathways to help state employees strengthen data literacy and improve government efficiency.

title: New York launches initiative to gather feedback to shape future of state ID portal
summary: The NYS Digital Access initiative launched Monday, inviting businesses and residents to weigh in on the future of the state’s online ID portal.

title: Nevada names its first chief privacy officer
summary: In the role, Casey Quinn will lead statewide privacy governance and data protection efforts for executive branch agencies.

title: New law adds satellite emergency alerts into federal warning system, but researchers question its impact
summary: The law could help people receive emergency alerts when cell networks fail, but experts say better technology alone won’t fix gaps in how warnings are sent.

title: Georgia Technology Authority unveils AI playbook for state’s local governments
summary: The playbook is intended to serve as a guide for cities and counties to adopt AI responsibly, particularly those that lack dedicated AI teams.

title: NASCIO: States shouldn’t wait to start preparing for cyber risks posed by quantum computing
summary: With quantum computing expected to emerge within the next decade, NASCIO is urging states to start taking the threats seriously.
